newsitem.title: INDIA: TATA IBM TO INTRODUCE NETWORK COMPUTERS TO INDIA.
newsitem.headline: TATA IBM TO INTRODUCE NETWORK COMPUTERS TO INDIA.

text.p: Tata IBM Ltd, a 50-50 joint venture between India's Tata group and International Business Machines Corp, will introduce the first network computer (NC) in India, the head of the company said on Friday.
"Tata IBM will introduce a network computer in India in September," Ravi N. Marwah, CEO and managing director, Tata IBM Ltd told Reuters on Friday.

Network computers are stripped down personal computers linked to a central data warehouse, allowing them to share conventional desktop functionality. This reduces the cost per machine to under $1,000.
Marwah said he did not foresee a big demand for network computers immediately, but expected it to pick up in the near future. Marwah refused to comment on the price of the network computer.

IBM introduced a range of new network computers in the U.S. last month called the Network Station series, with prices starting at $799. In India, the price is expected to be higher as import duties and local levies add 37.86 percent to the price of a computer.
Dataquest magazine's annal survey puts the size of the Indian market in 1996/97 (April-March) at 467,387 personal computers and 66,520 servers.
